newsitem.title: INDIA: Tibetan exiles rally for democracy in Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: Tibetan exiles rally for democracy in Hong Kong.

text.p: Indian police on Tuesday detained 32 Tibetan exiles who demonstrated outside the Chinese embassy, shouting support for the democracy movement in Hong Kong and demanding an independent homeland.
The protesters chanted "Democracy for Hong Kong, independence for Tibet", for about 40 minutes before police bundled them into trucks and took them to a police station in the capital.
They were all released two hours later, police said.

The demonstration, held on the first day of China's rule over Hong Kong since Britain relinquished control at midnight on Monday, was organised by the Tibetan Youth Congress, a 13,000-member non-governmental organisation of Tibetan exiles.

"Our endeavour is to show our support for democracy in Hong Kong. It is very important that democracy continues to live in Hong Kong, and that the Chinese see it in action," L. Pema Lhundup, joint secretary of the Tibetan Youth Congress, told Reuters.
"If democracy continues to thrive in Hong Kong, it will lead to an easier solution to the Tibet issue," Lhundup added. "Hong Kong gives us hope that there will be an end to our struggle in Tibet."
Rebellions and protests against Chinese rule have erupted periodically in Tibet since the 1950s when communist troops took control.
The Dalai Lama, Tibet's spiritual leader, fled his homeland to India in 1959 after an abortive uprising against Chinese rule. There are 130,000 Tibetans living in exile in India.
The Hong Kong handover has stirred bitter memories for many Tibetans who accuse Beijing of stealing their independence and reneging on promises.
"China continues to hold on to Tibet like any colonial appendage," the bureau of the Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, said in a statement at the weekend.
